bullets: How a push times its distance becomes work, how fast that work is done becomes power, and how energy changes form without ever being lost
slides.heading: Energy: work, power and conservation
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we push one crate, time it fast and slow, drop one mass, and learn to follow energy as it changes form.

bullets: Calculate work as force times distance and power as work divided by time
Track gravitational potential energy becoming kinetic energy and state why the total stays the same
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things.

bullets: A car burns through its petrol, rolls slower and slower, and stops - the tank is empty
So has all that energy been destroyed, or is it still somewhere?
slides.heading: Where does the energy go?
slides.notes: Ask for predictions and take two or three answers without judging them yet; say: the falling mass scene will settle it.

bullets: Work is a force times the distance it moves its object; power is how fast that work is done; energy is what work transfers from one form to another
Each quantity is a product or a ratio: change one part and the whole effect changes, even when the total energy never does
slides.heading: Work, power and conservation
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the map for the whole lesson: first the push, then the timing, then the fall.

bullets: A 50-newton force pushes a crate 4 metres along the floor, so the work done is 50 times 4 = 200 joules
If the crate does not move at all, the distance is zero and the work is zero, however hard the push
slides.heading: Work = force × distance. No movement, no work.
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: follow the crate along the floor, read the force and the distance off, and multiply them together.

bullets: The same 200 joules of work done slowly in 10 seconds gives a power of only 20 watts
Done fast in 2 seconds, the same 200 joules gives 100 watts - power measures how fast work is done
slides.heading: Same work, less time = more power. Power is work rate.
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: the work never changes, only the clock shrinks - and the power reading climbs fivefold.

bullets: A 2-kilogram mass held 5 metres up stores 98 joules of gravitational potential energy
Released, it falls: the GPE drains away as the KE grows, and at the bottom all 98 joules are kinetic - the total never changes
slides.heading: 98 J of GPE became 98 J of KE. Same total, different form.
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: watch the GPE bar empty into the KE bar, and keep asking where the total has gone - nowhere.

bullets: The car's chemical energy becomes kinetic energy plus heat as it moves; when the tank empties the car stops, but no energy has vanished
The total energy before equals the total energy after - energy changes form, it is never destroyed
slides.heading: Energy is transformed, not used up — conservation holds.
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: follow the petrol energy into motion and escaping heat, and name the total that stays the same.

bullets: Work = force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200 J for the crate push
Slow, in 10 s: power = 200 / 10 = 20 W. Fast, in 2 s: power = 200 / 2 = 100 W - same work, five times the power
slides.heading: Worked example: one push, two powers
slides.notes: Work this on the board slowly: write the work first, then divide it by each time in turn and compare the two powers.

bullets: A 30 N force pushes a box 5 m - find the work done, then the power if the push takes 3 s
Then open the worksheet: one work calculation, one used-up trap, one power question and a falling mass
slides.heading: Your turn
slides.notes: Give three quiet minutes for the first task, take answers from the class, then set the worksheet going in pairs.

bullets: Four questions: the used-up energy trap, a work calculation, a power comparison, and GPE becoming KE
Write one sentence: where does a car's energy go when the petrol runs out?
slides.heading: Exit ticket
slides.notes: Collect the tickets at the door; the first question revisits the trap head-on, so it shows straight away who still thinks energy can be destroyed.
